# Simulation

## Overview

Each `simulateShard` SLURM job runs `scripts/run_simulation_shard.py`, which:

1. Reads cohesin parameters and CTCF sites from `configs/parameters.py`
2. Builds the tiled polymer (`tiling:` in the config; by default 28 copies of the locus on 70,000 monomers)
3. Runs the **loop-extrusion factor (LEF) dynamics engine** for a burn-in period
4. Runs `polychrom` (OpenMM wrapper) to simulate 3D chromatin folding on a GPU
5. Writes trajectory blocks to `output/sims/{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{N}_shard{M}/`

With the default `sim_run.engine: polysim`, steps 3–4 are done by the Hansen
lab's polysim package; `polychrom` runs ChromSimPipe's original model (see
[Simulation engines](#simulation-engines)).

## Simulation engines

| Setting | `polychrom` (original; reproduces earlier runs) | `polysim` (default) |
|---|---|---|
| Model code | ChromSimPipe's own: Python LEF model (`scripts/lef_dynamics.py`) driving polychrom | The Hansen lab's [polysim](https://github.com/ahansenlab/polysim_bootcamp) (Cython LEF model + bond updater on polychrom), pinned in `envs/cohesin_sim.yml` |
| `lifetime` units | steps; each leg moves every step, so ~`lifetime` kb per leg | LEF timesteps (blocks); each leg moves with probability `vlef` per timestep, so ~`lifetime × vlef` kb per leg |
| Stalled cohesin | released with `ctcf_release` per step | lives `life_boost_stalled` × longer when both legs are stalled (`ctcf_release` unused) |
| Extrusion vs polymer motion | 1 LEF step per `md_steps_per_block` (250) MD steps | 1 LEF step per `poly_steps_per_block / vlef` MD steps (13,200 with the defaults) |
| Polymer | `polymer:` block (density 0.2, stiff chain) | `polysim:` block (density 0.3, flexible chain) |
| Saved frames | every block; no 3D warm-up | every `saveevery` blocks; optional unsaved equilibration (`initskip`) of at least one LEF lifetime |
| `total_blocks` means | blocks simulated per replicate | conformations saved per replicate |

For polysim, the shard runner maps each oriented CTCF site to polysim's stall
arrays (+ sites stop leftward-moving legs: `ctcf_left`; − sites stop
rightward-moving legs: `ctcf_right`), each with the condition's `ctcf_capture`,
seeds numpy and C `drand48` from the shard seed, and calls
`polysim.sim3d.run()` with the shard folder as output. polysim writes the same
`blocks_*.h5` files (plus the LEF bonds of each saved frame under `SMCs`), so
merging and analysis are unchanged. A `preparePolysim` job imports polysim once
before the shards start, so its Cython module is compiled once rather than by
every GPU job at the same time.

## The cohesin (LEF) dynamics engine (polychrom engine)

Loop extrusion factors (LEFs = cohesin rings) are simulated as pairs of one-
dimensional walkers on the polymer lattice.

```
5'─────────────────────────────────────────────────────3'
          ↑ cohesin loads randomly
          ├──►  ◄──┤  (two feet walk outward)
          │          │
          ▼          ▼
    ←CTCF◄          ►CTCF→  (stalling at oriented CTCF sites)
```

| Event | Rate | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Load | 1 / `separation` monomers | Poisson process, random position |
| Step | 1 monomer / LEF step | Each foot moves outward unless blocked |
| Unload (free) | 1 / `lifetime` | Geometric: ~75 steps = ~75 kb |
| Capture at CTCF | `ctcf_capture` = 0.125 | 12.5% per encounter |
| Release (stalled) | `ctcf_release` = 0.0033 | Per-step chance a stalled foot resumes; stalled rings still unload at 1 / `lifetime` |

### Oriented CTCF sites

CTCF stalls cohesin only from the correct (convergent) direction. The BED files
produced by the `orientCTCF` rule (`scripts/extract_ctcf_sites.py`) encode orientation as the FIMO motif strand:

- **Left-facing** CTCF (←): stalls a rightward-moving left foot
- **Right-facing** CTCF (→): stalls a leftward-moving right foot

Convergent CTCF pairs therefore trap cohesin between them, forming stable loops.

## The 3D simulation with the polychrom engine (OpenMM)

Each monomer is a bead. Forces between beads:

| Force | What it models |
|-------|---------------|
| Polymer chain bonds | Chromatin backbone (harmonic bonds + angle stiffness) |
| Excluded volume | Steric repulsion (soft sphere) |
| Spherical confinement | Nuclear membrane |
| **LEF bonds** | Cohesin-mediated loop (harmonic spring between extruded monomers) |

LEF positions are updated every `sim_run.md_steps_per_block` MD steps; each saved block is one
"snapshot" in the trajectory HDF5.

::: {.callout-note}
The OpenMM simulation runs on GPU. The SLURM job requests 1 GPU, 4 CPUs, and
60 GB RAM, set under `set-resources:` in `profiles/<site>/config.yaml`
(on Longleaf: `l40-gpu,volta-gpu,gpu` partitions, `qos: gpu_access`). All `simulateShard` jobs
(conditions × replicates × shards) can run in parallel.
:::

## Tiling trick

To get statistically robust contact maps from a short locus (1,960 monomers by
default), 28 copies are placed end-to-end on a 70,000-monomer polymer. Each copy folds
independently (boundary monomers are connected but distant in sequence), giving
28× the contact statistics per GPU run. After the simulation, contact maps from
all copies are averaged into one locus-sized map.

See Yang et al. 2023 *Nat Commun* for details on why this is valid.

## Entry point

```bash
python scripts/run_simulation_shard.py \
    --condition cond1_baseline \
    --replicate 1 \
    --shard-index 0 \
    --n-shards 4 \
    --output output/sims
```

Arguments come from Snakemake wildcards. Each job writes to:

```
output/sims/{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{replicate}_shard{shard}/
├── params.json        # all parameters, for reproducibility
└── blocks_*.h5        # HDF5 trajectory blocks
```

After all shards finish, `mergeShards` concatenates them:

```
output/sims/merged_{params_name}_ctcf-{sample}_rep{replicate}/
├── params.json
└── blocks_*.h5        # full trajectory (4 shards combined)
```
